conflicts.permit: Hugs N Hearts may respond to such question by using the Kid’s e-mail address.
conflicts.prohibit: Hugs N Hearts does not collect and does not permit Third Parties to collect from Kids any information that may personally identify an individual (e.g.name, address, e-mail)
conflicts.situation: A child uses the Kids App Ask a Question feature to e-mail a question, and the company receives and uses the child's e-mail address to reply.
conflicts.reason: Section 3.2 bars collecting e-mail from Kids and excepts only the persistent device identifier. Section 3.3 uses the Kid's e-mail. The Chapter A introduction mentions Section 3.3, but the 3.2 statement gives no carve-out.

conflicts.permit: You hereby agree that we may use the contact details you provided us to inform you regarding competitions we may hold, our new products and/or services, and to send to you other material.
conflicts.prohibit: The information abovementioned is collected and processed solely for the purpose of supporting Hugs N Hearts’ internal operations.
conflicts.situation: A child provides an e-mail address through the Kids App support feature, and the company considers sending news about competitions or new products to that address.
conflicts.reason: Chapter C applies to Kids Apps and permits marketing use of provided contact details. Chapter A limits Kid information to internal operations. Neither chapter states which governs for Kids Apps.

conflicts.permit: For avoidance of doubt, Hugs N Hearts may transfer and disclose Kids Non-personal Information to third parties at its discretion.
conflicts.prohibit: The information abovementioned is collected and processed solely for the purpose of supporting Hugs N Hearts’ internal operations.
conflicts.situation: The company discloses Kids Non-personal Information, such as gameplay and advertisement response data, to a third party for a purpose outside internal operations.
conflicts.reason: Section 4 permits disclosure at the company's discretion without a purpose limit. Section 3 says the listed Kid information is processed solely for internal operations. The policy does not say which statement governs.

conflicts.permit: We may transfer (and store) information collected about you, including Personal Information, to affiliated entities, or to other third party service providers across borders
conflicts.prohibit: We may share Personal Information only in the following cases:
conflicts.situation: An Apps for Everyone user's Personal Information is transferred to a hosting or other third party service provider abroad for ordinary business purposes.
conflicts.reason: Section 10 lists the only cases for sharing Personal Information and omits service providers. Section 20 permits transfer to third party service providers. Neither section refers to the other.

conflicts.permit: We cannot do all the things needed to make and run the Services by ourselves so we share information with third parties collectively called our ‘Partners’.
conflicts.prohibit: We will only disclose information with your consent where we are legally able.
conflicts.situation: Nitrome shares a player's device identifiers and behaviour data with advertising and analytics Partners without asking for consent.
conflicts.reason: The policy says it shares information with Partners to run the Services, and also says it will only disclose information with consent. It gives no exception for Partners and no precedence rule.

conflicts.permit: Nitrome and its Partners collect data from its Services automatically from the device, cookies, the service itself or from other Partner services we use.
conflicts.prohibit: This information is stored on your own computer and is not available to anyone else.
conflicts.situation: A player saves progress in a Nitrome Flash game, and the save data on the computer is among the progress data Nitrome and Partners collect automatically.
conflicts.reason: One section lists save-file progress among data Nitrome and Partners collect from the device. The Flash section says saved progress is not available to anyone else. The policy does not separate the games or data.

conflicts.permit: We may disclose Personal Data to our third party service providers to provide you with the Services, including our third party payment processor.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not sell, rent, or otherwise share your data to any third-party for a business or commercial purpose, other than the Auction House.
conflicts.situation: A Nevada resident buys an auction item, and the name, billing address and order total are sent to the third party payment processor.
conflicts.reason: The Nevada notice says data is shared with no third party other than the Auction House. The policy also discloses Personal Data to service providers and payment processors. The notice states no exception for service providers.

conflicts.permit: These partners may access your data and operate under their own privacy policies.
conflicts.prohibit: These partners process your data only at and according to Matchicard instructions to provide the Service, such as hosting, player support, advertising, analytics and fraud prevention.
conflicts.situation: An in-game advertising partner such as AdMob accesses a player's device identifiers and gameplay data.
conflicts.reason: One passage says advertising partners process data only on Matchicard instructions. Another says advertising partners operate under their own privacy policies. The policy does not say which advertising partners fall under each passage.

conflicts.permit: Firebase SDK, which is used for user’s preferences, favorite location storage and sending push notifications.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not disclose your information to third parties without your explicit consent except for the following purposes:
conflicts.situation: Transit sends a user's saved preferences and favorite locations to Firebase, a third party SDK provider, without asking for explicit consent.
conflicts.reason: Section 7 bars disclosure without explicit consent except for listed purposes, and none covers SDK service providers. Section 7.1 sends personal data to Firebase and other SDK providers. No stated exception connects the two.
